title.en: Civil Disobedience, Round Tables and the Poona Pact

text.en: On 6 April 1930 a 61 year old man bent down on the beach at Dandi and picked up a lump of salt. It was against the law, and it set the whole country on fire.

At Lahore in December 1929, with Jawaharlal Nehru as President, the Congress declared Poorna Swaraj as its goal.
26 January 1930 was declared Independence Day, and a pledge was taken across the country.
Gandhi sent Lord Irwin a charter of demands including abolition of the salt tax, and the Viceroy did not respond.
On 12 March 1930 Gandhi set out from Sabarmati with 78 followers and walked 241 miles in 24 days to Dandi.
At Dandi he broke the salt law by picking up salt on 6 April 1930, and C. Rajaji led a similar march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam.
In the North West Frontier Province Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan organised the Khudai Khidmatgar, the Red Shirts.
Women, peasants, tribals, students and children took part in the biggest mass movement India had yet seen.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 5 March 1931 released non-violent prisoners and allowed salt making, and Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference.
The Round Table Conference failed because Gandhi refused separate electorates for minorities.
Gandhi was arrested on 4 January 1932 when the movement was renewed, and the Congress did not attend the Third Conference.
On 16 August 1932 Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award giving separate electorates to minorities and the depressed classes.
Gandhi fasted unto death from 20 September 1932, and after talks with Ambedkar and M.C. Rajah the Poona Pact was signed.
It abandoned separate electorates but raised the reserved seats for the depressed classes from 71 to 148, and 18 percent in the Central Legislature.
Gandhi then led a campaign against untouchability, started the Harijan Sevak Sangh, and 8 January 1933 was observed as Temple Entry Day.

At Dandi on 6 April he broke the salt law.

why.en: Salt tax touched every household, so it united everyone.

text.en: Similar marches followed, such as Rajaji's to Vedaranyam.

prompt.en: What were the terms of the Poona Pact?

requiredIdeas.en: 18 percent of Central Legislature seats reserved

commonMisconceptions.en: Mixing up the Poona Pact with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact

points.en: Lahore 1929: Poorna Swaraj; 26 January 1930 Independence Day.
Poona Pact: joint electorate, seats up from 71 to 148.
